audit.why: TRICKY at 7/10 fits 45.45% over 308 Emerald+ games - the closest to even of my five, and the prose correctly frames it as a lane Mel can hold early and loses late.
audit.corrected: Left the rating. Only the TL;DR was replaced, because it was Kennen boilerplate claiming a poke mirror Mel usually wins.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Quinn levels 2, 3 and the first-item stage, and gave level 6 to Skill, against whys that say the opposite.
audit.why: whys[2] calls level 3 "a true coin-flip", whys[5] says the first-item stage stays "even", and whys[4] calls level 6 "your one clear lead" - that is Mel, not Skill. The packet chart matches the prose at every one of those stages and the stored chart did not.
audit.corrected: Chart re-proposed as one atomic group across both layers: Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Mel, Skill, Quinn.

audit.whatIsWrong: The blind is attributed to the wrong ability in both layers, repeatedly. The full layer names the focus ability "Vault (Dash/Blind)" and repeats that label in winCon, enemyWin, loading, tradeBad, the cooldown breakdown and all three dosFull entries. The content layer says "her E blind", "E blind plus Harrier" and "save E vault to blind your empowered autos". The full layer also instructs the player to "Reflect Vault back the moment he commits".
audit.why: Vault (E) is a dash that damages, slows, briefly interrupts and lands Quinn back near max attack range. It contains no blind. The blind is Blinding Assault (Q) - the name says so - on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 with 1025 range. Telling the player to fight when E is down to avoid a blind sends them into the actual blind. And Vault is a dash, not a projectile, so Rebuttal cannot reflect it. Also missing entirely: Behind Enemy Lines is a channel, so Solar Snare cancels it outright, which is how Mel answers the roaming that the late block correctly identifies as how she loses the game.
audit.corrected: Blind reassigned to Blinding Assault everywhere it appears, with its 11s cooldown. Vault restated as a dash and as her escape from the root at 12s. The reflect-the-dash instruction replaced with the Behind Enemy Lines channel cancel. Focus moved from E to Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad and dontsFull[2].d said Rebuttal is "gone for twenty seconds".
Nothing anywhere connected Quinn blind to Mel passive.
audit.why: Searing Brilliance loads up to nine bonus projectiles onto Mel next attack. A blind makes that attack miss, so the entire stored payload is thrown away on one whiffed swing. That is the single most punishing thing Blinding Assault does in this matchup and it was unwritten while the blind was being credited to the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Added as dosFull[0]: bank the nine projectiles past the blind rather than swinging through it.
